summary: Both core Theorem4.4 error bounds refuted by globally admissible genuine quantizer examples; bounded release activation-axis discrepancy.

problems.title: Both standard and compensated quantitative bounds are false
problems.assumptions: A=[1,0],norm1;c.01<.5;global four-bit two-dimensional quantizer relative bound2/225; exact initialization; deterministic independent inputs
problems.check: Original equation visual check; analytic global quantizer proof; separate parent Fraction recomputation
problems.counterevidence: Correct residual recurrence supports qualitative forgetting; no benchmark failure established
problems.impact: False quantitative theorem on main error-compensation dependency
problems.core_dependency: Section4.5 theoretically justifies suppression of accumulated error
problems.correction: Correct orientation(2c)^(k-t+1), telescoping and norm-sum bounds derived; no end-to-end theorem claimed

focused_check.note: Verified the genuine two-dimensional four-bit min/max quantizer, its uniform relative squared-error bound 2/225, legal constant/independent inputs and rank-one A. Both published bounds fail on the recorded admissible witness (3.992004 > 3.39006006; 0.998001 > 0.0452008008). Reversed unrolling and sign errors invalidate the core quantitative derivation, supporting Major; corrected recurrences preserve qualitative forgetting.

focused_check.note: Verified the 2x3x1x1 activation witness: the selected branch yields per-batch 2x1x1x1 parameters instead of per-channel 1x3x1x1. The act_tensor flag/default mapping is inconsistent with the description. This is Minor and release-scoped; the fixed tensorwise Stable Diffusion configuration and historical benchmark results are not refuted.
